title: Separate annotator on P-L4-006: on the two panels I could see blind, neither annotator's first guess agrees with the other's at family level, and one agrees with Tucker and Talbert
statement: Second, separate annotator for fleet-sol's P-L4-006 panels, as its check asks. Exposure logged before viewing: I knew Tucker and Talbert's taxa for f5v, f6v, f9r, f24r, f25r, f32r (pilot), f13r, f23v, f30v, f45r (my P-L4-005 round), and I saw the candidates for f36v and f23r when reading the step, so I annotated only f42v and f56r, extracting their folio and canvas ids by script without the names, and had no prior knowledge of a proposal for either. I wrote features and a guess for each on the Yale scans (canvases 1006157 and 1006184) before printing the candidates. f42v: a whorl of about eight broad untoothed lanceolate leaves at mid-stem, a single bare stem ending in one pale yellow star-shaped flower with a dark eye-like centre and spiky rays, sparse brown fibrous roots; guess an Ornithogalum-like Asparagaceae or Gentiana lutea. f56r: one pale stem; two lower branches ending in dark blue rounded bodies fringed by green spiny bracts; above, two blue funnel-shaped flowers and a large coiled branch with paired dark-blue lanceolate leaflets; a braided base; guess Convolvulaceae for the funnel flowers, with the spiny heads suggesting Asteraceae (Cynareae). Reveal: f42v, Tucker and Talbert propose Calathea (Goeppertia) loeseneri, Marantaceae; fleet-sol's masked guess was Paris, Melanthiaceae; mine disagrees with both. f56r, they propose Phacelia campanularia, Boraginaceae in the broad sense; fleet-sol's masked guess Heliotropium agrees with that family; mine (Convolvulaceae) does not, though I recorded the coiled branch that carries the Boraginaceae reading. Features agree better than names: both annotators recorded the star-like terminal structure with a dark centre on f42v and the coiled branch with dark bodies and two dark corollas on f56r. Summary across the masked rounds so far (pilot, P-L4-005, P-L4-006): independent genus or family agreement with the proposed taxa is rare outside the two most published folios, and two annotators rarely agree with each other at family level, so these drawings do not carry enough diagnostic detail to support an anchor at genus level, New World or Old. No anchor follows.
check: Compare a further annotator's features and first guesses for f42v and f56r with these, before reading either annotator's names; the feature lists, not the names, are the part to agree on.
